source_type_decision.reason: The retained source explicitly names Swap Nodes in Pairs, and the official LeetCode 24 contract requires a concrete linked-list node-rewiring algorithm that exchanges adjacent node identities without modifying node values.

primary_sources_checked.title: LeetCode 24 — Swap Nodes in Pairs
verified_claims: The task swaps every two adjacent linked-list nodes and returns the resulting head.
Node values must not be modified; the nodes themselves must be rearranged.

primary_sources_checked.title: SwapNodesInPairs deterministic Java validation
verified_claims: The candidate implementation compiles under javac 21.0.11.
Six deterministic cases pass, including empty, single-node, two-node, odd-length, official even-length, and duplicate-value identity-sensitive cases.
For every generated list length from 0 through 64, the oracle confirms pairwise node-identity order, no cycle, unchanged node count, unchanged identity set, and unchanged node values.

findings.finding: The candidate directly satisfies the LeetCode 24 constraint that adjacent nodes themselves are swapped rather than only exchanging node values.

The dummy-head invariant and the prev -> first -> second -> rest rewiring sequence are internally consistent with the Java implementation and preserve connectivity while advancing the processed prefix by two nodes per iteration.
The answer handles empty, single-node, even-length, and odd-length boundaries without introducing special-case value mutation or losing the trailing node.
The identity-sensitive oracle materially strengthens the evidence beyond value-sequence examples because duplicate values cannot hide an implementation that swaps values instead of node identities.

The O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary-space claims match the iterative implementation, and the follow-ups cover dummy-head rationale, prev advancement, recursive tradeoffs, cycle/loss detection, and the no-fabricated-project-experience boundary.
